dominant_breach: private credit and nonbank intermediation can hide leverage, valuation, and interconnectedness until public-stability tools are expected
fastest_washout: opaque credit losses jump from private contracts to pension/insurance/bank/systemic-risk channels

public_balance_sheet_gate.note: Rev0365 adds locator-bound materiality, counterparty, redemption, Form PF, and FSOC monitoring edges. The risk is now measurable enough for a serious stress map, but still not certified as a public loss because the waterfall and public-upside terms are absent.

private_credit_nonbank_interconnectednes.note: Evidence now includes FSB global size/interconnectedness, Fed U.S. size and semi-liquid vehicle figures, OFR counterparty-exposure estimates, and bank/NBFI monitoring surfaces. It supports an active risk perimeter, not a bailout verdict.

nonbank_resolution_and_liquidity_perimet.note: Resolution and liquidity perimeter remains blocked: redemption caps, Form PF confidentiality, delayed/amended reporting, and imperfect fund identification mean claimants cannot yet see who bears stress losses or what public tools would demand in return.

implicit_bailout_expectation.note: Implicit support pressure is plausible through bank commitments, insurer/pension/retail exposures, employment/borrower stress, and FSOC monitoring, but Rev0365 explicitly refuses to infer a bailout absent facility terms, haircuts, fees, recoveries, and public-upside recovery.

financial_stability_backstop_governance.note: FSOC and regulators are monitoring private credit and Form PF may improve identification of private-credit-active funds, but filings are confidential and proposed/delayed, so governance remains a currentness and transparency blocker.

proof_debt: actual Form PF/SEC/FSOC aggregate outputs after October 1, 2026 or any final reporting changes
fund-level or official aggregate leverage, liquidity mismatch, valuation marks, and redemption-gate data
bank, insurer, pension, retail, and LP commitment concentration by loss-bearing claimant
borrower default, PIK, amendment, valuation markdown, and employment effects under stress
explicit public liquidity, no-bailout, haircut, fee, recovery, and public-upside terms

gate_20_public_balance_sheet.why: Rev0365 adds materiality/counterparty/reporting edges but certification is blocked until stress-loss allocation, claimant priority, public-liquidity terms, and public-upside recovery are proved from primary instruments or official data.

evidence_debt_register.question: fund leverage, liquidity mismatch, and redemption-gate data
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Map leverage, NAV valuation, gate terms, outflows, and redemption caps by vehicle type, especially BDCs and interval funds.

evidence_debt_register.question: valuation markdown and covenant evidence under stress
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Compare reported valuations, defaults, covenant amendments, and borrower restructuring outcomes under a severe downturn.

evidence_debt_register.question: pension, insurance, retail, and end-beneficiary exposure
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Quantify who ultimately bears losses after fund, insurer, pension, and semi-liquid retail vehicle exposures are traced.

evidence_debt_register.question: bank financing, warehouse-line, and credit-commitment exposure
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Map bank commitments/outstandings to private-credit funds and BDCs and test spillover to bank funding or supervision.

evidence_debt_register.question: nonbank resolution and public liquidity no-bailout rules
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: State who is not protected, what conditions attach to any public tool, and what public-upside recovery applies.

20A_debt_interest_capacity.question: Do debt service and maturity/interest risks crowd out floors, services, enforcement, public investment, or countercyclical repair?
20A_debt_interest_capacity.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20B_claim_security.question: Are social-insurance, pension, health, disability, care, or public-benefit promises financed and legally durable enough to count as wealth substitutes?
20B_claim_security.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20C_contingent_liabilities_guarantees.question: Are guarantees, insurance funds, credit programs, SOEs, PPPs, disaster obligations, and legal claims disclosed and stress-tested?
20C_contingent_liabilities_guarantees.finding: Blocked until bank lines, insurer/pension allocations, semi-liquid retail vehicles, leverage, valuation, and borrower-credit concentrations are mapped as potential contingent public-stability liabilities.

20D_crisis_backstop_governance.question: Who is rescued under stress, under what terms, with what haircut, condition, sunset, and report?
20D_crisis_backstop_governance.finding: Crisis governance remains under-specified because private losses can route through banks, employment, retirement promises, insurer solvency, or market-functioning tools.

20E_public_upside_recovery.question: Does the public receive warrants, equity, fees, clawbacks, senior claims, recoveries, or other upside when it absorbs downside?
20E_public_upside_recovery.finding: Rev0365 makes public-upside recovery material rather than not applicable: any public liquidity, guarantee, market-functioning, or supervisory rescue channel must specify fees, haircuts, senior claims, clawbacks, warrants, recoveries, and claimant priority before comfort is possible.

20F_central_bank_quasi_fiscal_visibility.question: Are remittance losses, deferred assets, interest-on-reserves distribution, facilities, and asset-price stabilization effects visible?
20F_central_bank_quasi_fiscal_visibility.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20G_public_asset_sovereign_wealth_govern.question: Are public assets rule-bound, professionally managed, protected from raiding, and linked to ordinary claimants?
20G_public_asset_sovereign_wealth_govern.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20H_generational_intergovernmental_incid.question: Does repair fall on younger cohorts, renters, disabled claimants, caregivers, migrants, municipalities, or future taxpayers?
20H_generational_intergovernmental_incid.finding: Indirect losses can fall on retirement savers, insurance policyholders, portfolio-company workers, local tax bases, and future public capacity.

public_balance_sheet_register.legal_authority: Securities, insurance, pension, bank-supervision, resolution, and financial-stability authorities depending on stress channel
public_balance_sheet_register.claimant_perimeter: Borrowers, private-credit funds, BDCs, interval funds, fund managers, banks with credit commitments, insurers, pensions, retail investors, workers, policyholders, retirement savers, and public stability agencies
public_balance_sheet_register.maximum_exposure: At least the mapped private-credit market, bank commitments/outstandings, semi-liquid vehicle assets, insurer/pension allocations, and correlated borrower exposure; Federal Reserve estimates U.S. private-credit loans near $1.4T in late 2025
public_balance_sheet_register.expected_loss: Unknown because private valuation, leverage, covenant, exposure, and redemption data remain incomplete
public_balance_sheet_register.stress_scenario: Credit downturn with borrower defaults, markdown lag, redemption pressure in semi-liquid vehicles, bank-credit-line stress, and pressure for public market-functioning support
public_balance_sheet_register.funding_source: private fund capital, sponsor fees/carry, bank provisions, insurer/pension buffers, redemption gates, borrower restructuring, and possible public liquidity or macro-stabilization tools
public_balance_sheet_register.loss_sharing: Private sponsors, investors, and banks should absorb first loss; public tools only for bounded market-functioning spillovers with conditions and recoveries
public_balance_sheet_register.public_upside_recovery: Not standardized; require facility fees, penalty terms, clawbacks, supervision conditions, or equity-like recoveries for any public downside absorption
public_balance_sheet_register.ordinary_claimant_protection: Protect policyholders, pension beneficiaries, retail investors, workers, and public-service capacity without rescuing sponsor carry or valuation discretion
public_balance_sheet_register.sunset_or_review: FSB and domestic financial-stability monitoring cycles; annual or stress-event refresh after major defaults, redemption caps, or bank-exposure changes

seniority_waterfall.claimant: Senior secured private-credit lenders and fund structures
seniority_waterfall.notes: Collateral, covenants, and private restructuring can protect lenders before workers, suppliers, and local communities.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: Fund sponsors, managers, and institutional investors
seniority_waterfall.notes: Fees, carry, valuation discretion, and locked-in capital should not be public-protected.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: Pension, insurance, retail-fund, worker, and borrower-community claimants
seniority_waterfall.notes: They may bear losses through retirement/insurance promises, capped redemptions, portfolio-company restructuring, or reduced services.
Pressure emerges if bank credit commitments, correlated defaults, liquidity stress, or employment spillovers threaten market functioning.
